summary: Akira Momiyama works in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1972 to 1976 and was attested as a professor at Saitama University in 2005.

Akira Mukai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant in 1978, and was attested as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College in 1999.

Akira Omine was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at Kyoto University, studied under Kyoshi Takahama, and held professorships at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.
Akira Onda worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He served as a professor at Toyo University in 1974 and was attested as a professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo in 2002.

Akira Sadakata specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Akira Hirakawa, as well as the University of Paris, and served as an associate professor and professor at Tokai University.

Akira Saito is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the Australian National University, and held professorships at the University of Tokyo and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Akira Shimada specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, and under Daud Ali and Rajeev Lochan, later teaching at the State University of New York at New Paltz.

Akira Suganuma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University, where he served as an assistant and later as an associate professor (1991–1994), and also lectured at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda was a sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University and served as a professor at the University of Tokyo from 1965 to 1991.
Akira Yamada was a philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi from around 1944 to 1947. He held a post at Nanzan University from around 1951 to 1965.

Akira Yuyama was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Akitoshi Saito is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post as professor at Taisho University (attested 1982) and was later attested as professor emeritus there in 2014.
Akong Tulku Rinpoche was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1967, he founded the Kagyu Samye Ling Monastery and Tibetan Centre, where he was attested as abbot in 2009.
Akshay Ramanlal Desai was a scholar of history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Mumbai between 1937 and 1946 under the supervision of Govind Sadashiv Ghurye.
Alan Butterworth was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist. He was educated at Elizabeth College and Balliol College, Oxford, and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1883 to 1918.

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Temple University and served as a faculty member in the Department of Philosophy at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil, having also studied under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.
Alan Gowans was a scholar of history and archaeology. He was educated at the University of Toronto and completed studies at Princeton University in 1948 and 1950.

Alan John Bayard Wace was an archaeologist who studied at Pembroke College, Cambridge. He held posts at the British School at Athens, Victoria and Albert Museum, Alexandria University, and served as professor at the University of Cambridge.
Alan Lomax pursued studies at Choate Rosemary Hall, St. Mark's School of Texas, Harvard University, the University of Texas at Austin, and Columbia University.
